title: migrate() accepts 1-wei slippage floors, so the story's 'no zero slippage floors' rule gives no sandwich protection (up to ~5% of a full-holder migration extracted on fork)
storyRef: story-121 Technical Details, migrate step 1: "Require ... and **all four** min amounts `> 0` (Configuration Safety: no zero slippage floors)." Concerns: previewMigrate exists so "the UI ... derive[s] slippage mins".
description: The only on-chain slippage rule is `minSUSDSOut, minPhUSDOut, amountSUSDSMin, amountPhUSDMin != 0` (L232). The story's stated purpose for that rule is to forbid unbounded slippage, but a floor of 1 wei is accepted and is economically identical to zero. The Router02 add (L245-246) is then priced entirely by the V2 pair's live reserves, which a searcher can move in the same block. The contract is user-facing (any BPT holder, via Etherscan or the not-yet-built phlimbo-ui modal), and the safe floors exist only as an off-chain convention (derive from previewMigrate). The Balancer leg is not the exposure: the holder owns ~100% of BPT and swaps are blocked once the pool is paused.
impact: Fork 26,303,097, whole-holder migrate (12,036.97 BPT -> 11,096.40 sUSDS + 13,145.69 phUSD, ~22,206 sUSDS of value) with 1-wei floors: a 10,000 sUSDS front-run/back-run sandwich of the V2 add costs the holder 1,101.79 sUSDS (~5.0%) and nets the attacker +893.92 sUSDS. A 2,000-token sandwich costs 54.55-74.80 sUSDS. With floors set 50 bp under an unmanipulated previewMigrate, every 2,000 and 10,000 front-run reverts, and the small ones that fit inside the band lose the attacker money. The protection therefore works when floors are meaningful, and the remaining exposure comes from user-chosen floors. That keeps this at Low: it is borderline user-input under C4 rules, but the story asserts the opposite property, the consuming UI does not exist yet, and BIP-928 makes this the only exit for a ~$25k position.
evidence: side-effects.json migrateForkResults.sandwichOfV2Add; test_r43_sandwich_oneWeiFloors and test_r43_sandwich_50bpFloors in work/test/audit-run43/BalancerLPMigratorRun43.fork.t.sol; log evidence/run43-tests.log
recommendation: Make it a binding requirement of the phlimbo-ui migration-modal story that the four floors come from previewMigrate(bpt), read when the user signs, minus an explicit bounded tolerance (for example <= 50 bp), and that a short deadline is used. Optionally, harden the contract by adding the pair's reserve ratio as a caller-supplied bound, or by requiring the two Router02 floors to be at least (1 - maxBps) of the Balancer outs times the pair ratio. At minimum, amend the NatSpec and story text so 'non-zero' is not presented as slippage protection.
